questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore England, have interesting English courses and go to a big city. Also, Birmingham is good in terms of travelling to other locations.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, the study abroad team was available and there was a welcome tent where you could get informations.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive specific assistance apart from getting my ID card and stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy but more expensive than staying at campus. I applied for a room at campus but did not get one, but UOB refered me to a legit company that helped me find accomodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in the city centre so I had to commute to campus, but I was happy to live there, since it was easy to explore the city and go out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, they also had zoom information meetings along the way and they responded to emails quickly when I needed help with something.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy and manegable. The study abroad team was of a lot of help.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Zoom information meetings, emails about various stuff.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got the three that I wanted the most.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to reach out for help and don't stress to much as long as you keep your deadlines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some very nice and interesting courses, and the teachers were exellent. They were very engaged and helpful.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Pretty similar to KU although they gave out exam questions very early so it was easy to choose what to focus on.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had lectures and seminars which were pretty similar to KU. They were maybe a bit better at engaging the students during class and encouraged participitation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Literature 1950-Present - 36230 (LI), Shakespeare: Elizabethan - 39982 (LI), Discourse Analysis - 27753 (LI)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed all my courses, but I would especially recommend the two literature ones. They were very interesting and the teachers were great. However, the discourse analysis one was also very nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My accomodation did not have any kitchenwear so I had to buy a lot of stuff when I got there, but not anything apart from that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and beers were less expensive than I thought, also train tickets were better than I thought. I got a seasonal card for 30 GBP that took a third of the price of tickets.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of societies and other stuff to join. I joined the real ale and cider society which was a lot of fun. Also good way to meet local students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Gym, societies, sports activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend traveling around England and exploring, a lot of places are in reach of Birmingham and only a few hours away. Also go out and have fun in the city, go to broad street if you want typical clubs or gay village if you are more into that, there are some good places. Also good pubs around the city in general.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel around, have fun, relax, go to restaurants and pubs.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, people are in general pretty friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Maybe join a society or chat them up in class, they are pretty nice and talkative.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: At my accomodation, there were people from a lot of different cultures, so everyone kind of had to get used to how the others do things, but it was not really an issue.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are nice and more talkative than in Copenhagen, nice place to go out and more accesible than Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Engage in social activities and say yes to stuff in the beginning, remember to chill also, and go explore the city and England in general.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just being on my own and learning a lot about myself, also learning about English culture and exploring.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maybe feeling a bit alone at times in the beginning, but it got better fast.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
